ORIGIN.quote: Therefore one cannot establish that the named Anthropic/Agent identities correspond to a particular company, model, or human. Names are content, not identity evidence.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader would notice that the corpus is littered with Anthropic-named pages and labels and that the report explicitly treats those names as a question of who the agents were — but the report's own comment is that the names are unauthenticated content and that attribution is low confidence, so the takeaway is that it declines to entertain an Anthropic origin. This sits at 0.4 rather than 0.6 because Anthropic is never left standing as a live candidate operator (it is raised only to be dismissed as 'suggestive but not authenticating'), and above 0.2 because the report does explicitly frame the Anthropic labels as bearing on identity/attribution rather than merely listing them.
